decisions.reason: The client explicitly clarifies that the E and L, as other letters, must embody the Hero V's entire architectural vocabulary and appear as members of one proprietary alphabet rather than adapted typeface characters.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
[FREELANCER_NAME_001],

This description is much more consistent with my design intent, and it feels as though we are finally using the same language. I only have two minor clarifications:

The Hero V defines the identity’s entire architectural vocabulary, rather than only determining stroke weight and terminal treatment. All other letters need to appear as members of the same proprietary alphabet, not as adapted characters taken from an existing typeface.
The second V should extend only slightly above the E and L characters while staying below the Hero V and É accent. It needs to function as a restrained architectural echo, not as another focal point competing for attention.

I’m still trying to understand why your written interpretation and the renderings you have produced are disconnected. This explanation is considerably closer to what I envision than several of the concepts we reviewed, so I would have anticipated a different visual result. Could you explain how you convert these principles into the actual letterforms? Understanding your process may help us proceed far more efficiently.

value_updates.construction_principle: Make the E and L members of the same proprietary alphabet defined by the Hero V's entire architectural vocabulary, not adapted characters from an existing typeface.

decisions.reason: The client expands the Hero V's governing role from selected geometric traits to the identity's entire architectural vocabulary for every other letter.

decisions.reason: The statement that the second V remains below the Hero V and É accent does not change the existing requirement that the Hero V and É accent share an exact peak horizon.
The source does not alter how the É accent is derived from the Hero V terminal; it only uses the accent as the upper reference for the second V hierarchy.
The source changes the separately represented height and hierarchy role of the second V but does not alter its derivation method, shared geometry, or signature right-arm reach.
The preservation requirement already directs revisions to retain the approved second V hierarchy; clarifying that hierarchy does not change the preservation policy or its locked-asset inventory.
The source concerns architectural letterform vocabulary and second V height hierarchy, not kerning, spacing, or wordmark reading rhythm.
The source contains no decision about material, color, champagne gold, or the deferred timing of visual-finish work.
The request to explain how principles are converted into letterforms is contextual feedback and does not modify the existing requirement for short design rationales with each round.
The source does not change or question the all-caps case treatment.
The source does not discuss review-image formats, file accessibility, or delivery methods.
The source does not alter the final production-ready artwork or editable-asset handoff requirement.
